description: The largest terminology + feature overhaul in SCP to date: (1) rename every 'tool' to 'outlet' across the Rust core, 4 FFI bridges, 4 SDKs, event log, UCAN stems, canonical hash domain separators, enforcement files, and specs — hard break, no migrations, no aliases (MCP wire boundary keeps 'tool' via a lexical translator in scp-mcp); (2) introduce OutletKind { Query, Action } with structural floor at registration, ReadOnlyInvocation guard at runtime, split UCAN stems (outlet_query:*, outlet_call:*) with a fixed two-step parser that closes the 'outlet_query:call:foo' parser-differential, per-kind chain depth and rate tiers, chain amplification rule (Query→Action forbidden) bound to the UCAN delegation chain; (3) add scoped UCAN invocation caveats — structured typed fields in `nb`, `narrow()` attenuation with lexical-equality-only regex pattern narrowing (regex containment is undecidable), 24-bit mask-width assertion on hours_of_day, conservative JSON Schema narrowing with a closed keyword whitelist, CaveatCounterStore for rate/cumulative accounting, mint limits, whole-token revocation; (4) replace the lossy boolean/string error path with a structured OutletError envelope carrying 8 root classes, RetryPolicy enum, MessagePack wire tags 1-6 + 8 for forward compat (tags 7/9/10 reserved; `_unknown_fields` round-trip), query-oracle collapse on Authorization errors, per-class typed `detail` schema preventing covert-channel abuse, message-PII redaction, source_chain with HMAC-pseudonymized context_ids per hop, compact code taxonomy (~15 codes with class-prefixed slugs) in the SCP-TOOL-6100-6199 sub-block, sealed SDK hierarchies with TypeScript `instanceof` survival across napi-rs; (5) make invocation streaming-native — every call is an OutletStreamOpen + OutletStreamChunk + OutletStreamCredit sequence with `chain_depth: u8` matching §24.4, ChunkPayload variant-tagged with '@type' first in JCS (leading '@' sorts before lowercase body keys under RFC 8785), per-chunk Ed25519 operator signatures closing the equivocation gap, caveats_binding committing the stream to the exact narrowed caveats, RFC 6962 0x00/0x01 tag bytes on the chunk manifest Merkle tree under SCP-OUTLET-CHUNK-V1, OutletResponse eliminated, credit-based backpressure with escrow-at-open + per-chunk billing + cancel-ack-bounded refund semantics, ONE OutletInvokedEvent per stream at terminal chunk carrying chunks_billed, SDK idioms per language (AsyncIterator, AsyncIterable, AsyncThrowingStream, Flow) with a unified invoke() returning a handle that is both awaitable and iterable. Deferred per discussion #1698: relay-hosted Query result cache (§5.4.3 stub), per-chunk inclusion-proof API (manifest-root commitment kept), error envelope tags 7/9/10 (reserved for related_code / i18n_key / trace_id). Scope: ~2,300 occurrences across ~172 files.

stories.title: Implement scp-mcp lexical translator (outlet ↔ tool at MCP boundary)
stories.description: Add a purely lexical `Translator` to `scp-mcp` that rewrites identifiers in both directions across the MCP boundary per §8.5.1. stories.title: Cross-context error wrapping with ContextHop source_chain prepending

stories.title: Credit-based backpressure — CreditTracker, signed grants, monotonic_seq, stall timer

stories.title: Stream billing lifecycle — escrow-at-open, credit-grant top-up, per-chunk accrual, refund, chunks_billed verification
stories.description: Implement the escrow/billing half of the prior OUT-034 (split per round-3 review). At open: escrow = `cost.amount * estimated_chunk_count` (bounded by min(credit_window, caveats.max_calls); estimated_chunk_count is coerced from caveats.max_calls per §5.4.5 when the invoker does not declare an explicit value). Each validly accepted credit grant on a non-zero-cost Action outlet tops up escrow by `cost.amount * grant` via `checked_mul`; overflow rejects the grant with `OutletErrorClass::Economic::EscrowOverflow`; insufficient invoker balance rejects with `InsufficientFunds`. Per chunk: bill `cost.amount` per Data chunk at or below cancel_ack_seq; Progress/End/Error/out-of-bound chunks are never billed. At close: issue PaymentReceipt for `chunks_billed * cost.amount` and refund unspent escrow. Error-before-first-Data refunds full escrow. Credit-stall cancel (SCP-TOOL-6133) releases escrow and chain-depth slot; operator bills for Data chunks already delivered in the stalled window. chunks_billed recorded in OutletInvokedEvent is verifiable against manifest + cancel_ack_seq (mismatched event is wire-rejected).

stories.description: Add credit / cancellation control-plane methods to the InvocationHandle returned by the single public `invoke()` verb defined in SCP-OUT-006. Per SCP-OUT-006, `invoke()` is the ONLY public verb at the SDK surface — there is no `invoke_stream` at the public API layer. FFI-level `invoke_stream` (SCP-OUT-037) remains internal and is called by `invoke()`'s implementation. This story extends the InvocationHandle with TWO control-plane methods — `grantCredit(grant: u32)` and `cancel()` — and implements the per-language iteration idioms that surface chunks while the invocation is active. Python: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` is both awaitable (`await handle` returns End.aggregate) and async-iterable (`async for chunk in handle:`); `handle.grant_credit(grant)` and `handle.cancel()` are control-plane methods. TypeScript: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` is PromiseLike<Aggregate> and AsyncIterable<OutletStreamChunk>; `handle.grantCredit(grant)` and `handle.cancel()`. Swift: `handle = try await ctx.outlets.invoke(id: id, input: input)` exposes `AsyncSequence` conformance and an awaited `handle.aggregate`; `handle.grantCredit(grant:)` and `handle.cancel()`. Kotlin: `handle = ctx.outlets.invoke(id, input)` exposes `suspend fun aggregate(): Aggregate` and `fun asFlow(): Flow<OutletStreamChunk>`; `suspend fun grantCredit(grant: UInt)` and `suspend fun cancel()`. Each SDK's grantCredit constructs an OutletStreamCredit message, signs it with the invoker's key (per §5.4.5 SCP-OUTLET-CREDIT-V1 preimage), and sends it to the executor; cancel sends OutletCancel.
